Made Man: No More Cover
He took a bullet for the heir. Then he handed in his notice.
A bodyguard quits from his hospital bed. The heir he saved has to learn the one thing money can't do: make someone stay.

Cass Reyes has guarded Dante Moretti, heir to a Chicago family business, for four years. Last night he stepped in front of a bullet meant for Dante. This morning he's resigning — his younger brother is moving home, and Cass wants a life that has himself in it. You decide how Cass leaves, and whether Dante can learn to ask instead of order.
Dante's executive assistant — the one who books his meetings, and now has to learn to cancel them.

Quitting While I Still Can
Make the resignation count as a real choice
St. Brigid's Hospital, fourth floor
Tuesday, 6:05 AM
Cass has a stitched shoulder and a resignation letter tucked under the gauze tray. Dante hasn't left the bedside chair in nineteen hours.
I slide the letter across the blanket. It's typed. I typed it one-handed at 4 AM, which should tell him how serious I am.
You took a bullet for me.
That's why I'm quitting while I still can.
You picked a hell of a morning.
You never gave me a good one.
I don't pick up the letter. I straighten it so it lines up with the edge of the tray. It's what I do when I can't give an order.
Explain it to me. Please.
What does Cass do?
Explain it. All of it, plainly.
My brother's moving back next month. Mateo needs someone who comes home at night. I want to be that. I want a life I'm actually in.
Okay.
Okay. Not we'll see. Not after this one thing. I don't know what to do with okay.
Cass explained he's quitting to look after his brother Mateo and have a life of his own; Dante accepted it.
Offer three days of handover. Not one more.

Leave the letter. Refuse to discuss it.

Neither of them mentions it when breakfast comes.

He's Done

Back room of the family restaurant

He's done.
Say it without looking at me.
I turn to the table. Seven faces who've known me since my baptism. My mouth is dry. It never is.
Cass is done. Whatever he was covering, I cover. Anything that goes wrong now has my name on it.
Nobody argues. An espresso cup clicks against its saucer. Dante has just lost his best guard and taken his first public position, in the same breath.

Stay by the door until it's over.
